description: Rewrote the closing sentence of the top-level summary, which claimed the entry 'captures the extracted claims... without yet normalizing, relating, or assessing them,' contradicting the fully populated normalized_claims, relations, and assessment_layer already present. Replaced with accurate language describing the entry's actual current content and continued unverified status.

Changed basis from 'asserted_in_source' to 'inferred_across_sources' and basis_source_ids from ['src_010'] to ['src_009','src_010']; rewrote notes to clarify the opposition between NC_015 and NC_014 is drawn from comparing the two source texts rather than stated by src_010 itself, since no src_010 excerpt explicitly engages Plaga's 'differing assumptions' framing.

Changed basis from 'asserted_in_source' to 'inferred_across_sources' and basis_source_ids from ['src_012'] to ['src_009','src_012']; rewrote notes to note that the src_012 excerpt's 'Ref. [4]' most plausibly refers to Casadio & Harms's own earlier work rather than Plaga's src_009 paper, so the cross-claim link to NC_009 is an analyst inference rather than an in-source assertion.

Added FF_015 (source_incentive_pressure for src_011) and FF_016 (source_incentive_pressure for src_012) to correct the asymmetric application of this failure-mode category noted in AF_004, since incentive-pressure concerns had been raised for src_001, src_002, src_009, and src_010 but not for src_011 or src_012 despite plausible motives documented in their own evidentiary_role/limitations. Extended AN_004 to reference the new flags and note the partial (not complete) resolution of the asymmetry.

Lowered FF_008 severity from 'critical' to 'significant' to match FF_007, since both flags describe the identical direct_evidence_absent failure mode applied to opposing positions (NC_001 vs. NC_011) and no rationale was documented for weighting the risk-side claim more heavily. Updated notes to record the correction.

Investigated the claimed dangling/mismatched cross-reference in the source packet's lhc_c001.relevant_claims field. Confirmed the mismatch exists only in the external packet's excerpt-level metadata (not part of the Case schema) and that this Case's own extraction_notes correctly attribute EC_004 to lhc_c002 and NC_012 to EC_027/src_009. No content in the Case was altered; added a dismissed AuditNote documenting the review and reasoning, per the rule to record why an alleged defect was not 'fixed' when it does not apply to the object being repaired.

Restored the dropped qualifying phrase 'from such black holes' to the quoted Giddings-Mangano conclusion in NC_019's normalized_text and in FF_012's notes, matching the verbatim excerpt text (lhc_c014/EC_039) instead of the truncated quotation, to avoid subtly broadening the quoted claim's scope.

Corrected location.page values to use pdf_page (per the convention used elsewhere in the draft, e.g. EC_020/EC_021/EC_024): EC_032-EC_035 (from lhc_c012, pdf_page=2) changed from '1' to '2'; EC_036 (from lhc_c013, pdf_page=3) changed from '2' to '3'.

Removed the unlicensed elaborative clause 'i.e., on a timescale far shorter than needed to travel any macroscopic detector distance,' which was not present in or supported by the underlying extracted claim (EC_001) or its source excerpt (lhc_c001), restoring a normalization closer to minimal paraphrase of the source text.

Removed 'NC_017' from AS_001.well_supported_claim_ids. NC_017 carries only medium confidence, is explicitly hedged as a subjective literature-awareness claim ('to our knowledge'), and is separately flagged by FF_013 for lacking a specified consensus dependency basis; categorizing it as well-supported was internally inconsistent with these documented caveats.
